title: Tessa Busby
dek_or_short_description: PKD's fourth wife. Met in July 1972 in Fullerton, California; married 1973. Mother of Christopher Kenneth Dick. Separated 1976.
body_markdown:
Tessa Busby (also known as Leslie) entered PKD's life in July 1972 in Fullerton, California, at a critical moment — after the break-in investigation and as PKD was beginning to process the 2-3-74 experiences. They married in 1973 and had a son, Christopher Kenneth Dick, also born that year.

By the time of the *Selected Letters*, Tessa appears in co-signed letters, indicating she was living with PKD and deeply involved in his daily life. However, the marriage was brief; they separated in 1976. Despite the short duration, the relationship fell during one of PKD's most creatively intense periods — the composition of the *Exegesis* was underway, and PKD was grappling with the theological and metaphysical aftermath of March 1974.

Like Nancy Hackett, Tessa represented PKD's ongoing struggle to maintain intimate relationships while consumed by paranoia, religious obsession, and literary ambition. The letters suggest a man trying to build domestic stability even as his inner world grew increasingly turbulent and strange.
summary: Tessa Busby (1973–1976), PKD's fourth wife. Met in Fullerton in July 1972; married 1973. Mother of Christopher Kenneth Dick. Marriage brief but concurrent with PKD's intense Exegesis composition period.
